Nirmit can do 2/3 of a job in 18 days. Kashish is twice as efficient as Nirmit. In how many days Kashish will complete the job?
questions.solution:
Since Kashish is twice as efficient as Nirmit

⇒ Kashish can do 2/3 of work in 18/2 days

⇒ 2/3 of work can be done in 9 days

⇒ whole work can be done in 9 × (3/2)

∴ Kashish can do whole work in 27/2 days

questions.question: An article is listed at Rs. 2375. A man purchases it at two successive discounts of 50% and 25% and spends Rs. 165 on repairing of article. If he sells the article at a profit of 62.5%, then what is the selling price (in Rs.) of the article?
questions.solution:
Man bought that article can be given as

⇒ 2375 × (1 – 50/100) × (1 – 25/100)

He bought it for Rs. 890.625

Price of article after repairing = 890.625 + 165

Price after repairing is Rs. 1055.625

Price of article after 62.5% profit can be given as

⇒ 1055.625 × (1 + 62.5/100)

⇒ 1055.625 × 1.625

⇒ 1715.39

∴ selling price be Rs. 1715.39

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a cuboid are in the ratio 19 : 11 : 13. If length is 30 cm more than height, then what is the volume (in cm³) of this cuboid?
questions.solution:
Let their length, breadth and height be 19y, 11y and 13y respectively

From the problem statement

⇒ 19y = 30 + 13y

⇒ 6y = 30

⇒ y = 5 … (i)

Volume is given as length × breadth × height

⇒ Volume = 19 × 11 × 13 × y³ [Using (i)]

⇒ Volume = 19 × 11 × 13 × 5³

∴ Volume is 339625 cm³

questions.question: Average age of a team having 12 players is 23 years. If the age of the coach is also included, then the average age increases by 2 years. What is the age (in years) of the coach?
questions.solution:
Average is given as sum of ages of all players/12 players

⇒ 23 = sum of ages of all players/12

⇒ sum of ages of all players = 12 × 23

⇒ sum of ages of all players = 276 … (i)

After adding the age of coach average is 25(23 + 2)

⇒ (sum of ages of all players + age of coach)/13 = 25 Using (i)

⇒ 276 + age of coach = 25 × 13

⇒ Age of coach = 49

∴ coach’s age is 49 years

questions.question: An item is sold at two successive gains of 30% and 20%. If the final selling price is Rs. 31200, then what is the cost price (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
Let its cost price be Rs. x

Price after two successive gains can be written as

⇒ x × (1 + 30/100) × (1 + 20/100) = 31200

⇒ x × 1.3 × 1.2 = 31200

⇒ x = 20,000

∴ the cost price is Rs. 20000

questions.question: Aman and Kapil starts from Delhi and Gwalior respectively towards each other at same time. They meet at Mathura and then take 196 minutes and 225 minutes respectively to reach Gwalior and Delhi. If speed of Aman is 30 km/hr, then what is the speed (in km/hr) of Kapil?
questions.solution:
Let us assume that the distance between Delhi and Mathura be p km and between Mathura and Gwalior be q km and speed of Kapil be s km/hr.

Since both of them started at same time and reached Mathura at same time, means time taken by them is same

⇒ time = distance/ speed

⇒ time taken by Kapil to reach Mathura = time taken by Aman to reach Mathura

⇒ q/s = p/30 ….(i)

For Aman to reach Gwalior,

⇒ q = 30 × 196/60

⇒ q = 98 …..(ii)

For Kapil to reach Delhi,

⇒ p = s × 225/60 Using (i) and (ii)

⇒ q/s = 98/s = s × 225/(60 × 30)

⇒ s = √{98 × 60 × 30/225}

∴ Speed of Kapil be 28 km/hr.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**For such types of questions, 

We can use the direct formula as,

⇒ Speed space of Aman over Speedspace ofspace Kapil = √ {Timespace takenspace byspace Kapil overspace Timespace takenspace byspace Aman}

⇒ 30/K = {sqrt{{225over60}over {196over60}}}

⇒ 30/K = (5 × 3)/14

⇒ K = 28

**∴ Speed of Kapil = 28km/hr.**

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money for 10 years is Rs. 3130. If the principal becomes 5 times after 5 years, then what will be the total interest (in Rs.) obtained after 10 years?
questions.solution:
The principle gives 3130 as interest in 10 years. Implies it gives 1565 interest in 5 years. 

After 5 years the principle is 5 time. The interest for remaining 5 years is also 5 times = 5 × 1565 = 7825. 

Total interest we get at the end of 10 years= 7825 + 1565= 9390

questions.question: If (x + y)² = xy + 1 and x³ – y³ = 1, then what is the value of x – y?
questions.solution:
Given (x + y)² = xy + 1

⇒ x² + y² + 2xy = xy + 1

⇒ x² + y² + xy = 1 ---- (1)

Since we know that x³ – y³ = (x - y)( x² + y² + xy), now using (1)

⇒ x³ – y³ = 1 = (x - y)( x² + y² + xy),

⇒ x – y = 1

∴ x – y = 1

questions.question: ABCD is a parallelogram in which AB = 7 cm, BC = 9 cm and AC = 8 cm. What is the length (in cm) of other diagonal?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ab5ab66c5ec8422d50bed93191def9eb03be772076ca9b41be5137a88f82eb78.png] 

By parallelogram Formula of diagonals,

AC² + BD² = 2 (AB² + BC²)

⇒ 8² + BD² = 2 (7² + 9²)

⇒ 64 + BD² = 2 (49 + 81) = 260

⇒ BD² = 260 – 64 = 196

⇒ BD = 14 cm

∴ The length of other diagonal = 14 cm

questions.question: How many diagonals are there in octagon?
questions.solution:
Concept used:

Number of diagonals for n sided polygon is given as = ⁿC₂ – n

⇒ For octagon n = 8

⇒ ⁸C₂ – 8 = (8!/(8 - 2)! × 2!) - 8 = (8 × 7 × 6!/(6! × 2)) - 8 = 56/2 - 8

⇒ 28 - 8

∴ 20 diagonals are in a Octagon

questions.question: A square is inscribed in a quarter circle in such a way that two of its vertices on the radius are equidistant from the centre and one vertice lie on the circumference. If the side of square is √(5/2) cm, then what is the radius (in cm) of the circle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of square = AB = BC = CD = DA = √5/2 cm

**Concept used:**

The diagonal of the square will be the radius of the circle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/984032aad9f529dc43a551913401b85085cb36f70d87803774b3c7532737c279.png] 

Let radius of quarter circle be r.

⇒ Side of square = √(5/2) cm

Using Pythagoras Theorem in ΔABC,

⇒ r² = (side)² + (side)²

⇒ r² = {√(5/2)}² + {√(5/2)}²

⇒ r² = (5/2) + (5/2) = 5

⇒ Radius of circle = r = √5 cm

**∴The radius of the circle is √5 cm.**

questions.question: If sec²θ + tan²θ = 5/3, then what is the value of tan2θ?
questions.solution:
**Concept used: **

sec²(x) = 1 + tan²(x)

**Calculation:**

⇒ sec²θ + tan²θ = 5/3

⇒ 1 + tan²θ + tan²θ = 5/3

⇒ 2tan²θ = 2/3

⇒ tanθ = 1/√3

⇒ θ = 30

**∴ tan(2θ) = tan(60) = √3**

questions.question: A tower is broken at a point P above the ground. The top of the tower makes an angle 60° with the ground at Q. From another point R on the opposite side of Q angle of elevation of point P is 30°. If QR = 180 m, then what is the total height (in metres) of the tower?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/606a4e080450c479fabe50699cd414310e5e798abd29841ea02441b7c7e08b49.png] 

Let the height of the broken tower be h and RO be y

QR = RO + OQ

⇒ OQ = 180 - y

⇒ In ΔRPO,

tan30° = PO/RO

⇒ 1/√3 = h/y

⇒ y = √3 h ----(i)

Now in ΔPOQ,

⇒ tan60° = PO/OQ

⇒ √3 = h/(180 - y)

Using (i)

⇒ √3 = h/(180 - √3 h)

⇒ 180√3 - 3h = h

⇒ h = 45√3 m

⇒ y = √3 h = √3 × 45√3 = 135 m

In ΔPOQ,

sin60° = PO/PQ

⇒ √3/2 = h/PQ = 45√3/PQ

⇒ PQ = 90 m

Total height of the tower = PO + PQ = h + PQ = 45√3 + 90 = 45(√3 + 2) m

questions.question: If sinθ + sin5θ = sin3θ and 0 < θ < (π/2), then what is the value of θ (in degrees)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sinθ + sin5θ = sin3θ

⇒ -sin θ = sin5θ - sin3θ

**Calculation:**

Using identity in RHS sin(x) – sin(y) = 2 × cos{(x + y)/2} × sin{(x – y)/2}

⇒ – sin θ = 2 × cos(4θ) × sin(θ) 

⇒ cos(4θ) = -1/2 = cos(120)

⇒ 4θ = 120

**∴ θ is 30**
